description: CTE alignment with Snowflake across three areas: COLUMN ALIASES in the definition, RECURSIVE CTEs, and CTEs inside UPDATE / DELETE / MERGE / INSERT. A definition's column list renames the projected columns, over a literal projection, over a table's own columns and over an aggregation alike. The RECURSIVE keyword is OPTIONAL: a CTE that references its own name as a table source recurses with or without it - requiring the keyword made a keywordless closure fail with 'Table does not exist', the shape production transitive-relationship loaders use. Self-reference detection is by the PARSE TREE, a FROM-item named like the CTE, so a CTE named like a column, a function, or a substring of other text stays non-recursive. Converted 1:1 from query/CTEAlignmentTest (now retired); the Java asserted a row COUNT for most recursive cases and read one or two indexes for the rest, and the converted tests assert the whole ordered row set - the factorial series is now pinned at every step rather than only at 6! = 720, and the transitive closure names its six pairs rather than counting them.

steps.sql: WITH cte(a, b) AS (SELECT 1, 'hello') SELECT a, b FROM cte
CREATE TABLE nums (x INTEGER, y INTEGER)
INSERT INTO nums VALUES (10, 20)
WITH cte(val_a, val_b) AS (SELECT x, y FROM nums) SELECT val_a, val_b FROM cte
CREATE TABLE sales (dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
INSERT INTO sales VALUES ('A', 100), ('A', 200), ('B', 300)
WITH dept_totals(department, total) AS (SELECT dept, SUM(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY dept) SELECT department, total FROM dept_totals ORDER BY department
WITH counter AS (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM counter WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM counter ORDER BY n
CREATE TABLE edges (src VARCHAR, tgt VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO edges VALUES ('a1','a2'),('a2','a3'),('a3','a4')

WITH walk AS (SELECT src AS parent, tgt AS child, ARRAY_CONSTRUCT(src, tgt) AS vec FROM edges UNION ALL SELECT w.parent, e.tgt, ARRAY_APPEND(w.vec, e.tgt::VARIANT) FROM walk w JOIN edges e ON w.child = e.src WHERE NOT ARRAY_CONTAINS(e.tgt::VARIANT, w.vec)), dedup AS (SELECT DISTINCT parent, child FROM walk) SELECT parent, child FROM dedup ORDER BY parent, child
CREATE TABLE vals (r INTEGER, rr INTEGER)
INSERT INTO vals VALUES (1, 10), (2, 20)
WITH r AS (SELECT r, rr, UPPER('rush') AS s FROM vals) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM r
WITH RECURSIVE counter(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM counter WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM counter ORDER BY n
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, manager_id INTEGER)
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', NULL)
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (2, 'Bob', 1)
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (3, 'Charlie', 1)
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (4, 'Dave', 2)

WITH RECURSIVE org(id, name, manager_id) AS (SELECT id, name, manager_id FROM employees WHERE id = 1 UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id FROM employees e JOIN org ON e.manager_id = org.id) SELECT name FROM org ORDER BY id
WITH RECURSIVE fact(n, f) AS (SELECT 1, 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1, f * (n + 1) FROM fact WHERE n < 6) SELECT n, f FROM fact ORDER BY n
WITH RECURSIVE nums(val) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT val + 1 FROM nums WHERE val < 3) SELECT val FROM nums ORDER BY val
CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER, price DOUBLE, category VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO products VALUES (1, 100.0, 'A'), (2, 200.0, 'B'), (3, 150.0, 'A')
UPDATE products SET price = price * 0.9 WHERE id IN (WITH discounted AS (SELECT id FROM products WHERE category = 'A') SELECT id FROM discounted)
SELECT id, price FROM products ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE items (id INTEGER, active BOOLEAN, score INTEGER)
INSERT INTO items VALUES (1, true, 10), (2, false, 20), (3, true, 30)
UPDATE items SET score = score + 5 WHERE id IN (WITH active_items AS (SELECT id FROM items WHERE active = true) SELECT id FROM active_items)
SELECT id, score FROM items ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE logs (id INTEGER, level VARCHAR, message VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO logs VALUES (1, 'INFO', 'msg1'), (2, 'ERROR', 'msg2'), (3, 'INFO', 'msg3')
DELETE FROM logs WHERE id IN (WITH to_delete AS (SELECT id FROM logs WHERE level = 'INFO') SELECT id FROM to_delete)
SELECT id, level FROM logs ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, total DOUBLE)
DELETE FROM orders WHERE id NOT IN (WITH high_value AS (SELECT id FROM orders WHERE total >= 100.0) SELECT id FROM high_value)
SELECT id, total FROM orders ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE target (id INTEGER, val VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO target VALUES (1, 'old1'), (2, 'old2')

MERGE INTO target t USING (WITH new_data AS (SELECT 2 AS id, 'updated2' AS val UNION ALL SELECT 3 AS id, 'new3' AS val) SELECT id, val FROM new_data) s ON t.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET val = s.val WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, val) VALUES (s.id, s.val)
SELECT id, val FROM target ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE series (n INTEGER)
INSERT INTO series WITH RECURSIVE s(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM s WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM s
SELECT n FROM series ORDER BY n
